title: WPSS/1632/2015 of Jot Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(1) Writ Petition (S/S) No.1631 of 2015
Kamal Singh ÖÖ. Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ....Ö. Respondents
(2) Writ Petition (S/S) No.1632 of 2015
Jot Singh ÖÖ. Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ....Ö. Respondents
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal with Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, Advocates for both the petitioners.
Mr. BPS Mer, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for the Uttarkhand Public Service Commission.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Both these petitions, with a minor variation, are
identical in nature and hence, are being taken up together
for hearing and disposal.
 Petitioners namely Kamal Singh and Jot Singh
applied for the posts of Sanitary Inspectors under the
general category pursuant to the advertisement dated
1.10.2011, as amended on 23.11.2012. The total number
of posts were -65- out of which -38- were for general
category candidates. In the general category seats,
reservation was applicable as per rules and also in light of
the Constitutional Bench Judgment of Honíble Apex Court
in the case of Indra Sawhney vs. Union of India (AIR 1993
SC 477), the candidates belonging to reserved classes viz.
scheduled castes, scheduled tribes and other backward
classes had to be adjusted on the seats of general category
in case they over-score the lowest scoring general category

2
candidate. The minimum benchmark for general category
candidates, as adverted, was ë45í and for reserved class
categories of SC/ST/OBCs, it was ë35í. Petitioners Kamal
Singh and Jot Singh scored ë49í and ë46í respectively viz.
above the benchmark. Thus, both the candidates, though
scored above the cut off marks, but could not qualify in the
Final Select List, as unfolded by the Public Service
Commission issued on 30.6.2015.
 Petitioner Kamal Singh claims himself to be a
handicapped candidate, wherefor three percent reservation
was envisaged by the relevant government order. On this
score, the plea of Kamal Singh is not tenable for the reason
that one handicapped person has already been selected by
the Commission.
 It was argued that three percent of total number
of posts would carry at least ë2í posts for the handicapped
persons, so even after selecting one handicapped
candidate, petitioner Kamal Singh can be adjusted. The
Court feels that even if such an argument is accepted for a
moment, then both the seats, for handicapped persons, will
fall in the bag of general category candidates, which ought
not to be the intention of the reservation policy.
 As regards the pain of petitioners that despite
securing the marks above benchmark, they have been
ousted from the select list, the Court finds that the Rules
have duly been complied by the Public Service Commission
which contemplates about validation of taking away the
seats of general class category from the reserved class
category persons if the latter overscore the candidate of
general candidate at the bottom of the list. To this effect,
on a perusal of Annexure No.10, it transpires that the

3
candidate bearing roll no.102391 is a reserved class
candidate, who has secured -52- marks whereas no general
candidate has been declared successful scoring less than
such number of marks. Applying this formula, all the ë38í
posts, which were meant for general category candidates,
but due to over-scoring by the reserved class category
candidates, those have been declared as filled up in the
result.
 The remaining seats, which have still been left
un-filled out of the reserved class candidates, are obviously
for the reason that such candidates could not qualify the
minimum benchmark in such category.
 In view of what has been stated hereinabove, I
find that both these petitions have no force at all and thus,
the same are dismissed at the threshold. (Interim relief
applications 9258/15 and 9259/15 also stand rejected
accordingly)
